questions.solution_text:
Let $\alpha=\arcsin\frac{4}{5}$ and $\beta=\arctan\frac{5}{12}$.
Both arguments are positive, so both angles are in quadrant 1 and every ratio is positive.
$\sin\alpha=\frac{4}{5}$ and $\cos\alpha=\frac{3}{5}$
$\sin\beta=\frac{5}{13}$ and $\cos\beta=\frac{12}{13}$
$\cos(\alpha+\beta)=\cos\alpha\cos\beta-\sin\alpha\sin\beta$
$=\frac{3}{5}\times\frac{12}{13}-\frac{4}{5}\times\frac{5}{13}$
$=\frac{36}{65}-\frac{20}{65}$
$=\frac{16}{65}$

questions.question_text: Which expression equals $\sin\left(2\arccos x\right)$ for $-1\le x\le 1$?

options.why: Used $\sqrt{1+x^{2}}$, the hypotenuse of the $\arctan$ triangle, instead of $\sqrt{1-x^{2}}$.
This is $\cos\left(2\arccos x\right)$, obtained from the cosine double angle identity rather than the sine one.
Read $x$ as $\sin\alpha$ and applied $1-2\sin^{2}\alpha$, which is $\cos\left(2\arcsin x\right)$.

questions.solution_text:
Let $\alpha=\arccos x$, so $\cos\alpha=x$.
$0\le\alpha\le\pi$, so $\sin\alpha\ge 0$ and $\sin\alpha=\sqrt{1-x^{2}}$.
$\sin 2\alpha=2\sin\alpha\cos\alpha$
$=2\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\times x$
$=2x\sqrt{1-x^{2}}$

questions.solution_text:
Let $\alpha=\arcsin x$ and $\beta=\arccos x$.
$\sin\alpha=x$ and $\cos\alpha=\sqrt{1-x^{2}}$
$\cos\beta=x$ and $\sin\beta=\sqrt{1-x^{2}}$
$\sin(\alpha-\beta)=\sin\alpha\cos\beta-\cos\alpha\sin\beta$
$=x\times x-\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\times\sqrt{1-x^{2}}$
$=x^{2}-\left(1-x^{2}\right)$
$=2x^{2}-1$

questions.solution_text:
Let $\alpha=\arccos\left(-\frac{7}{25}\right)$, so $\cos\alpha=-\frac{7}{25}$.
$0\le\alpha\le\pi$ and $\cos\alpha<0$, so $\alpha$ is in quadrant 2.
$\text{opposite}=\sqrt{25^{2}-7^{2}}$
$=24$
The sine is positive in quadrant 2, so $\sin\alpha=\frac{24}{25}$.
$\sin 2\alpha=2\sin\alpha\cos\alpha$
$=2\times\frac{24}{25}\times\left(-\frac{7}{25}\right)$
$=-\frac{336}{625}$
